summary: Word of Yahweh comes to Jonah son of Amittai: Arise go to Nineveh great city cry against it, for wickedness has come up before me. But Jonah rises to flee to Tarshish from presence of Yahweh, goes down to Joppa, finds ship to Tarshish, goes down into ship, goes down into hold to sleep. Yahweh hurls great wind, mighty tempest, ship about to break, sailors fear each cries to his god, cast cargo to lighten, Jonah down in hold fast asleep, captain wakes: what do you mean sleeper? Call on your god. Sailors cast lots, lot falls on Jonah, interrogate who are you, where from, Jonah says Hebrew, I fear Yahweh God of heaven who made sea and dry land, told them he fled from presence, sailors fear, ask what to do, Jonah says throw me into sea and sea will be calm for I know this storm for my sake, sailors row hard to return, cannot, cry to Yahweh do not let us perish for this man's life, throw Jonah, sea stops raging, sailors fear Yahweh, offer sacrifice and vow.
whyItMatters: Satirical story about reluctant prophet who flees from presence of Yahweh — impossible since God made sea and dry land. Shows God's mercy extends even to enemies (Nineveh), and prophet is more pagan than pagans at start.

context.author: Anonymous
context.audience: Israel after exile, grappling with mercy to enemies
context.date: Set ~750 BC under Jeroboam II; composition debated — 8th-century tradition or post-exilic (~400 BC)
context.setting: Joppa port to Tarshish (Spain, far west) opposite Nineveh (east)
context.literaryForm: Satirical prophetic short story, with down motif

keyVerses.text: But Jonah rose up to flee to Tarshish from the presence of Yahweh. He went down to Joppa, and found a ship going to Tarshish; so he paid its fare, and went down into it, to go with them to Tarshish from the presence of Yahweh.
keyVerses.why: Key word flee from presence — impossible mission, comedic.

keyVerses.text: He said to them, “I am a Hebrew, and I fear Yahweh, the God of heaven, who has made the sea and the dry land.”
keyVerses.why: Confession while fleeing God of sea and land by sea — irony.

keyVerses.text: Then the men feared Yahweh exceedingly; and they offered a sacrifice to Yahweh and made vows.
keyVerses.why: Pagans convert while prophet flees — satire.

themes: pagan sailors more pious than prophet
God hurls wind then appoints fish

questions.question: Where is Tarshish and why does Jonah flee there?
questions.answer: Tarshish likely Tartessos in Spain, far west edge of known world, opposite direction of Nineveh (east, in Assyria, modern Iraq). To flee to Tarshish from Israel means go to Joppa port and sail west as far as possible. Text says flee from presence of Yahweh — ironic since Psalm 139 says no place to flee from Spirit, especially not sea since Yahweh made sea and dry land (Jonah's own confession v9). Comedy: prophet tries to escape omnipresent God by boat.

questions.question: Why does text repeat Jonah went down?
questions.answer: Hebrew yarad — down — appears: went down to Joppa, went down into ship, went down into inner part of ship to sleep. Four downs, plus later down into fish belly, down to roots of mountains. Pattern shows descent physically and spiritually — running from call is downward spiral. Then will need to be brought up. Literary device highlighting Jonah's disobedience as downward movement.

questions.question: Why are sailors more pious than prophet?
questions.answer: Satirical reversal: sailors each cry to his god (v5), try to lighten ship (responsible), don't want to kill Jonah — row hard to return (v13), pray to Yahweh not to charge innocent blood (v14), then fear Yahweh exceedingly and vow after sea stops (v16). Jonah sleeps in storm while pagans pray. Prophet is supposed to represent God but is least faithful; pagans respond rightly. Sets up theme: mercy outside Israel.

questions.question: What does casting lots mean and why does lot fall on Jonah?
questions.answer: Lots = like dice to discern divine will, common ancient practice, even in Israel (Achan story). Sailors ask whose fault storm, cast lots, lot falls on Jonah — providential pointing. Then interrogation: who are you, occupation, country, people — Jonah says Hebrew, fear Yahweh who made sea and dry land — confession that his own God of sea is hurling storm. His theology correct, behavior not.

questions.question: Why does Jonah say throw me into sea? Is it suicide or sacrifice?
questions.answer: Jonah says pick me up throw me into sea and sea will be calm for I know storm for my account. Can read as self-sacrifice, acceptance of judgment, or continued attempt to die rather than go to Nineveh — prefer death to obeying mercy to enemies. Sailors resist — row hard to return — more merciful than prophet. Eventually they pray and throw, sea stops. Jonah's action leads to sailors' conversion, ironically fulfilling prophetic role despite self.
